title: Washington, DC man sentenced to 80 months for multi-state pharmacy burglaries

Washington, DC man sentenced to 80 months for multi-state pharmacy burglaries
Deontae Britton has been sentenced to more than six years in federal prison for participating in pharmacy burglaries across three states earlier this year. Authorities say he conspired with others using forcible entry tools to steal controlled substances from multiple locations.
A Washington, DC man was sentenced on Oct. 7 to 80 months in federal prison for his role in a conspiracy that targeted pharmacies across Maryland, Pennsylvania, and Virginia.
U.S. District Judge Stephanie Gallagher imposed the sentence on Deontae Britton, also known as Deaundre Blount, who will also serve three years of supervised release following his prison term. Britton, age 33, was convicted of conspiring to break into 20 different pharmacies between January and April 2022.
According to court documents, Britton worked with Harold Dorman of Chillum, Maryland, and William Sherod III of Ft. Washington, Maryland, in a series of burglaries that prompted a tri-state investigation involving multiple law enforcement agencies. During each incident, two masked individuals—including Britton—entered the pharmacies after hours dressed in dark clothing. Sherod acted as a lookout from a separate vehicle nearby.
The group used tools such as a blue pry bar and a large silver Halligan bar—a forcible entry tool typically used by firefighters—to break into the stores. These methods caused damage to doors and locks at each location. Once inside, they remained for less than two minutes before stealing controlled substances including Oxycodone HCL, Promethazine-Codeine syrup, Hydrocodone-Acetaminophen, Adderall, Suboxone, and fentanyl patches for unlawful distribution.
Sherod received a sentence of 40 months in prison with three years of supervised release; Dorman’s case is still pending. U.S. Attorney Kelly O. Hayes commended federal agencies including the Food and Drug Administration (FDA), Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI), Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA), as well as numerous local police departments from Maryland, Pennsylvania, and Virginia for their assistance in the investigation.
The U.S. Attorney for the District of Maryland serves nearly six million residents across Maryland; it prosecutes federal crimes such as these burglaries while handling civil cases for the United States government and collecting government debts, according to its official website. The office employs over 200 personnel across its divisions and is part of the U.S Department of Justice.
